West Central St. Johns County in northeastern Florida...

* Special Marine Warning for...
Northeast Florida coastal waters from St Augustine to Flagler Beach
out to 60 NM...

* Until 600 PM EDT.

waterspouts was located 7 NM east of Marineland, or 10 NM northeast
of Palm Coast, moving east at 10 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

Big Georges Reef.

properties.areaDesc: San Diego County Coastal Areas; Orange County Coastal
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 5 at 1:33PM PDT until October 9 at 11:00PM PDT by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous rip currents
expected. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding
expected.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County
Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, from Tuesday afternoon
through Friday evening. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 6
AM Wednesday to 11 AM PDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only isolated
road closures expected. Minor coastal erosion is also expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Elevated surf of 3-6 feet, with sets to 7
feet, on south and southwest-facing beaches. High tides are
expected to peak between 6.5 and 7.0 feet during the mornings
and evenings.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous swimming conditions.

properties.description:
SMWTAE

The National Weather Service in Tallahassee has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Coastal Waters From  Ochlockonee River to Apalachicola FL out to 20
Nm...
Coastal Waters from Mexico Beach to Apalachicola out 20 NM...
Coastal waters from Okaloosa-Walton County Line to Mexico Beach out
20 NM...
Waters from Mexico Beach to Apalachicola FL from 20 to 60 NM...
Waters from Okaloosa-Walton County Line to Mexico Beach from 20 to
60 NM...

* Until 600 PM EDT/500 PM CDT/.

* At 357 PM EDT/257 PM CDT/, severe thunderstorms capable of
producing waterspouts were located along a line extending from 16
nm east of Mexico Beach to 11 nm south of Port St. Joe to 34 nm
west of Empire Mica Wreck, moving east at 20 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can quickly form and capsize boats...damage
vessels...and create suddenly higher waves. Make sure all
on board are in a secure location and wearing life
jackets. Expect wind gusts in excess of 34
knots...suddenly higher waves...frequent lightning...and
heavy downpours. Make sure all on board are wearing life
jackets.

* Locations impacted include...
Empire Mica Wreck, Apalachicola, Cape San Blas, Mexico Beach, St
George Island, and Port St. Joe.
properties.instruction:
Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.
